current.text: Myles Turner is expected to start at center for Milwaukee to open the season.
Milwaukee traded for Kel'el Ware, who competes with Turner for frontcourt minutes. One preseason projection started both of them, but the newest one starts Kuzma next to Turner.
Experts are split on whether Ware cuts into his minutes. One thinks the new teammate may limit him. Others think Turner and Ware can play together, and one still rates Turner above Ware.
Doc Rivers is no longer the coach. Experts largely blame Rivers for Turner's poor last season, when he was often benched in fourth quarters for Jericho Sims. Taylor Jenkins is the new head coach.

Experts disagree on a bounce-back. One calls him a strong bounce-back candidate, with about 29 minutes and top 60 upside. Another expects him to be only a little better than last year. A third says that at 30 he may simply be washed.
His motivation is a question after a miserable season in which he looked like he had lost confidence. If he gets 30 minutes, 2.2 blocks and 2.5 threes, he is easily a top 70 player.
Experts call him overpriced at picks 86 to 97. They see fair value around picks 100 to 128, and the newest call is fine at picks 110 to 120.
In one auction mock, the expert valued him at 1 to 3 USD and he sold for 6 USD.
Milwaukee's rotation is among the least clear in the league. It has too many guards, Jenkins' rotations are unpredictable, and he may use a deep rotation.
Milwaukee is expected to put more focus on developing young players as the season goes on. That would cut veteran minutes, and the starting lineup could change by December or March.
Milwaukee is expected to be a bad team, at about 33 wins, and the roster is expected to need trades to consolidate.
Milwaukee plays 14 back-to-backs, with 334 team games through March 28.

durable.text: His fantasy value rests on blocks and threes. Blocks are a league outlier, and he makes many threes for a center.
He is a poor rebounder for a center, gives almost no assists, and his FG% is weak for his position.
He needs good point guard play in the pick and roll. He suffers when he is parked in the corner.
He is worth less in points leagues than in category leagues.

note: Turner costs almost nothing in the markets now: a value of 1 USD and a 1.1 USD average cost on Yahoo, 3 USD and 1.8 USD on ESPN. Our league paid 20 USD for him last season, and he sold for 6 USD in one mock. He fits punt FG% builds that want blocks (projected 1.7 per game, z +2.3) and about 2 threes from the center spot, and he is a reasonable late buy at 1 to 5 USD. Early in the season, check whether his minutes reach about 29 to 30 and where Ware fits under Jenkins. Also check whether his blocks get back above 2 per game.
